chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who intends to recite a chapter (surah) but recites another instead, he said: 'He may go back to the point between where he stopped and where he would have finished two-thirds of it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one makes a mistake while reciting a Surah during prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical concession (rukhsah) in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the continuity of prayer over rigid perfection when a minor recitation error occurs. It reflects the juristic principle of facilitating worship by allowing correction within the same rak'ah, provided the error is rectified before completing two-thirds of the surah. This highlights the balance between reverence for the Quranic text and the reality of human error during devotional acts.
